distinguishing_features: Passive discrete high-density mass blocks locally alter the span's modal mass without changing pipe-wall thickness
The added mass lowers the first natural frequency to below the vortex-shedding frequency and outside the stated lock-in ratio
Verification is proposed using already-recorded flow and pressure signals rather than added sensors
parsed.objective_technical_problem: Reduce span fatigue caused by vortex-induced lock-in by passively detuning the span's natural frequency from the shedding frequency while avoiding active control and new instrumentation.
parsed.viable_reason: Although mass loading can shift natural frequency in principle, the stated pressure-fluctuation test is not reliably feasible because generic recorded line pressure may not contain a resolvable 1 Hz shedding component, and the massive attachments could introduce unacceptable local stresses and fatigue at their interfaces.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: A skilled engineer would readily consider passive mass loading as a routine way to detune a structure, with the selected mass and placement calculated from the modal-frequency relationship.
